constant.comment: -Infinity and -NaN are single literals in jsonv (a leading + is not accepted before either).
constant.name: constant.language.jsonv

number.comment: Every numeric literal jsonv accepts: optional sign; hex/binary/octal with an optional n; decimal integers with an optional n; decimals with a trailing dot (1.) or leading dot (.5); an exponent; and _ separators between digits.
number.name: constant.numeric.jsonv

reference.comment: An internal reference: an identifier, optionally followed by .member accesses (a.b.c). One region, so the one-shot #value in #arrayelement / #dictionaryvalueelement consumes the whole chain. Like the jsonv parser, it allows whitespace, comments and line breaks around each dot. The region ends at the first following token that is neither a dot nor a comment.
reference.name: meta.reference.jsonv

patterns.comment: a dot whose member name follows a comment or a line break
a dot not followed by a member name
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.expected-property-name.jsonv

patterns.comment: \x and \u without the full count of hex digits are the only escapes the jsonv lexer rejects
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.unrecognized-string-escape.jsonv

patterns.comment: any other escaped character is accepted as that character (\q is q), and a backslash before a line break is a line continuation
patterns.name: constant.character.escape.jsonv

patterns.comment: unquoted identifier key, including $/_-prefixed names and the keywords true/false/null/Infinity/NaN; the colon may follow after inline block comments
patterns.name: support.type.property-name.jsonv

patterns.comment: numeric key: any number literal jsonv accepts (decimal, signed, leading/trailing-dot, exponent, hex, binary, octal, bigint), or -Infinity / -NaN
patterns.name: support.type.property-name.numeric.jsonv

pendingobjectkey.comment: An unquoted identifier or numeric key with nothing but whitespace and comments after it on its line, so #objectkey's colon lookahead cannot see whether a ":" follows. The region spans lines until the ":" (left for the object's value rule). A "," or "}" that arrives first is flagged: the "}" is consumed here and the object then closes on its (?<=\}) end. Anything else before the ":" is flagged too.

arrayelement.comment: A single element's own region, freshly located -- via the array's own ongoing, per-line pattern search, which is what lets this find the element wherever it is (even many lines after "[" or a ",") -- by a zero-width lookahead at the element's actual start. \G inside always anchors there regardless of line breaks, because this region is entered fresh for every element instead of being reused across the whole array.

patterns.comment: the element itself, matched exactly once

an element no #value pattern recognizes (+Infinity, _1, a lone -). Consuming it keeps this region from opening and closing at the same position, which would stop vscode-textmate tokenizing the rest of the line.
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.unrecognized-value.jsonv

patterns.comment: anything else found where "," or "]" was expected -- still recursed into #value so a nested array/object stays balanced and properly scoped underneath the invalid wrapper
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.expected-array-separator.jsonv

object.comment: The (?<=\}) end alternative closes the object when #pendingobjectkey has already consumed its "}"; no other rule matched directly in this region ends with "}".
object.name: meta.structure.dictionary.jsonv

dictionaryvalueelement.comment: The object value's own region, freshly located (same technique as #arrayelement) by a zero-width lookahead at the value's actual start, so \G anchors correctly even when the value is pushed to a line after the ":".

patterns.comment: the object value itself, matched exactly once
a value no #value pattern recognizes; see the same rule in #arrayelement
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.unrecognized-value.jsonv

patterns.comment: anything appearing where "," or "}" was expected -- e.g. an orphaned key:value pair caused by a missing comma. The key (if any) is still recognized via #objectkey.
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.expected-dictionary-separator.jsonv
